newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary energy hike boosts MOL shares.
newsitem.headline: Hungary energy hike boosts MOL shares.

text.p: Hungarian oil and gas company MOL Rt shares rose sharply on the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) on Friday on the back of Thursday's energy price increases, dealers and analysts said.
"MOL's shares traded on the SEAQ have reacted to the news on Thursday and the Hungarian market adjusted prices accordingly," Zsolt Katona of ING Barings told Reuters.
On Friday, MOL shares closed at 1,755 forints, up 80.
More than 470,000 MOL papers changed hands in what one dealer said was over-enthusiastic trading.
"This is a psychological, overheated thing," said Peter Haas of Postabank Securities. "It is not yet clear what MOL's share will be from the price increase."
Hungary's government announced on Thursday that gas prices would go up by 18.8 percent for consumers on January 1.
Final details, including how the increase would be shared between wholesale and retailers are unlikely to be announced before mid-December, the MEH said.
ING Barings' London-based analyst, Gabor Sitanyi said MOL would probably be allowed to raise its producer price by around 15 percent, or five-sixths of the consumer price increase.
He said MOL is likely to get the lion's share of the rise as retail distributors are already profitable while MOL has been making losses on gas sales.

"Even if retailers only get one-sixth of the increase, their margin would still rise to seven forints per cubic metre from the current six forints, while MOL at current prices has lost some 2.4 forints per cubic metre (in the first nine months of 1996)," Sitanyi said.
MOL incurred these losses as it imports gas at near-market prices, while it has to sell at state-regulated prices.
Katona said that MOL's actual share of the price increase could make a significant difference.
"We have different scenarios depending on the distribution of the rise, with ratings from long-term buy to sell," he said.
